Sambir Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Sambir's Jews played a remarkably prominent role in the city's public and political life — by 1910, more than half of the city council's members were Jewish. In 1891, the city opened a Jewish commercial school, the only educational institution of its kind in all of Galicia to be granted government-institution status; it became a gymnasium in 1931. On February 13, 1943, about 500 Jews were murdered directly at this cemetery; a memorial was erected at the execution site in 2001. This is the older of Sambir's two Jewish cemeteries, presumed to have already been operating in the 17th century.
